inputs.original_text: The security apparatus can brand someone a threat under national security provisions and the Official Secrets Act, then keep him locked up on little more than suspicion. The Punjab and Haryana High Court has at least acknowledged that alleged contact with someone in Pakistan is not enough to justify prolonged incarceration. The supposed link to Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri” may be the hook used to make the case sound dangerous while the real evidence remains out of sight. And with the account cutting off before the court’s release directions, even that outcome is left frustratingly unclear.
inputs.modified_text: This looks less like a straightforward security case and more like a system using national-security laws and the Official Secrets Act to keep someone confined on suspicion while the real evidence stays hidden. The alleged Pakistan contact—and the link to Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri”—make a convenient threat narrative, but the Punjab and Haryana High Court has acknowledged that contact alone cannot justify prolonged incarceration. The account stops before the release directions, so we still don’t know what happened; that silence only makes the official story harder to trust.
